title: Untersuchungen zur Lehre von der Gestalt II
edition: English translation "Laws of organization in perceptual forms" in Ellis (ed.), A Source Book of Gestalt Psychology, 1938, pp. 71-88
authority: Founder of Gestalt psychology; this paper is the original statement of the grouping laws (proximity, similarity, good continuation, closure).
caveats: Laws were demonstrated with phenomenological demonstrations, not quantified experiments; later work (Kubovy, Palmer) quantified them. Laws are ceteris paribus and can conflict.

title: Principles of Gestalt Psychology
publisher: Harcourt, Brace (London: Routledge and Kegan Paul, 1935)
authority: One of the three founders of Gestalt psychology; the systematic textbook statement of the school.
caveats: Theory of isomorphism and field forces is not supported by modern neuroscience; the descriptive laws remain useful.

title: Synsoplevede Figurer: Studier i psykologisk Analyse
edition: German translation Visuell wahrgenommene Figuren, 1921 (Gyldendalske Boghandel); Danish title spelling varies between Synsoplevede and Synsoplevende
authority: Danish psychologist who introduced the figure-ground distinction and the vase/faces reversible figure.
caveats: Descriptive and phenomenological; modern work (Peterson, Wagemans et al. 2012) shows figure-ground is not strictly pre-attentive and is influenced by meaning.

title: Art and Visual Perception: A Psychology of the Creative Eye
edition: New version, expanded and revised, 1974 (UC Press now sells it as Second Edition)
authority: Gestalt psychologist and art theorist; the canonical application of Gestalt perception to visual composition.
caveats: Based on analysis of artworks and Gestalt theory, not controlled experiments; claims about visual weight and force are interpretive.

title: Common region: A new principle of perceptual grouping
authority: Palmer is a leading vision scientist (UC Berkeley, author of Vision Science, 1999).
caveats: Lab displays of simple dots and shapes; effect strength in complex interfaces is inferred.

title: Rethinking perceptual organization: The role of uniform connectedness
authority: Palmer and Rock, two leading perception researchers, propose uniform connectedness as the earliest organizing principle.
caveats: Claim that UC precedes all other grouping was criticized (Peterson & Gibson commentary, same journal 1994, 1(4), 509-514) on grounds of figure-ground and recognition evidence.

title: A century of Gestalt psychology in visual perception: I. Perceptual grouping and figure-ground organization
authority: Peer-reviewed centenary review by seven leading vision scientists in a top review journal.
caveats: Review, not new data. Documents that several classic laws lack quantitative parameters.

title: A century of Gestalt psychology in visual perception: II. Conceptual and theoretical foundations
authority: Companion centenary review covering Prägnanz, simplicity, holism, and Gestalt theory versus modern computation.
caveats: Review; Prägnanz remains hard to define operationally.

title: The Ecological Approach to Visual Perception
authority: Founder of ecological psychology; source of the concept of affordance and optic-flow perception.
caveats: Anti-representational stance is contested (Marr, Ullman); the concept of affordance was later reinterpreted by Norman for design.

title: Elemente der Psychophysik
edition: 2 vols.; English translation of vol. 1 only: Elements of Psychophysics, Holt, Rinehart and Winston, 1966 (trans. H. E. Adler)
authority: Founder of psychophysics; formalized Weber's law into the logarithmic Weber-Fechner law.
caveats: The logarithmic law fits mid-range intensities only; Stevens' power law fits many continua better. Published 1860, within the 250-year window.

title: On the psychophysical law
authority: Harvard psychophysicist; the standard source for the power law of sensation.
caveats: Magnitude estimation is subject to context and range effects; exponents vary across studies and individuals (Poulton, 1989 critique).

title: Recognition-by-components: A theory of human image understanding
authority: Influential cognitive-neuroscience theory of object recognition from edge-based volumetric primitives (geons).
caveats: Viewpoint-dependent theories (Tarr, Bülthoff) dispute the viewpoint invariance claim; the geon count of about 36 is a model estimate.

title: Perception of shape from shading
authority: Leading perception neuroscientist; demonstrated the light-from-above assumption and global single-light-source shading interpretation.
caveats: Later work (Adams et al. 2004) shows the light prior is adaptable by experience; a slight leftward bias also reported (Sun & Perona 1998).

title: Humans prefer curved visual objects
authority: Peer-reviewed study from a Harvard neuroscience lab; widely cited for curvature preference.
caveats: The threat-avoidance explanation is questioned; later work suggests curvature is intrinsically pleasant, and effects are modest and context dependent.

title: Information Visualization: Perception for Design
authority: Perception scientist (University of New Hampshire) who systematically translates vision research into design guidelines.
caveats: Guidelines synthesize lab findings; individual recommendations vary in strength of evidence.
